question: What are the three main states that files can reside in in Git?
expected_answer: Modified, staged and committed.

gold.evidence: Git has three main states that your files can reside in: _modified_, _staged_, and _committed_

question: How long is the checksum string Git uses to identify content?
expected_answer: A SHA-1 hash: a 40-character string of hexadecimal characters.

gold.evidence: This is a 40-character string composed of hexadecimal characters

question: Which file does git config use when given the --system option, and what privilege is needed to change it?
expected_answer: [path]/etc/gitconfig (values for every user on the system); changing it needs administrative/superuser privilege.

gold.evidence: If you pass the option `--system` to `git config`, it reads and writes from this file specifically. Because this is a system configuration file, you would need administrative or superuser privilege to make changes to it.

question: How can I read the full manual for the configuration command without an internet connection?
expected_answer: Run `git help config` (or `git config --help` / `man git-config`); manpages work offline.

gold.evidence: you can get the manpage help for the `git config` command by running this

question: What two kinds of tags does Git support?
expected_answer: Lightweight and annotated tags.

gold.evidence: Git supports two types of tags: _lightweight_ and _annotated_.

question: If I push using the --follow-tags option, which tags reach the remote?
expected_answer: Only annotated tags.

gold.evidence: if you use `git push <remote> --follow-tags` only annotated tags will be pushed to the remote.

question: I committed too early and forgot to include a file. How do I redo that last commit?
expected_answer: Stage the forgotten changes and run `git commit --amend`.

gold.evidence: stage them, and commit again using the `--amend` option

question: Under what condition is it safe to amend a commit?
expected_answer: Only when the commit is still local and has not been pushed.

gold.evidence: Only amend commits that are still local and have not been pushed somewhere.

question: What single guideline sums up the danger of rewriting history with rebase?
expected_answer: Do not rebase commits that exist outside your repository and that people may have based work on.

gold.evidence: Do not rebase commits that exist outside your repository and that people may have based work on.

question: Why does Git only move the branch pointer ahead when merging a hotfix that is directly ahead of master?
expected_answer: Because there is no divergent work to merge; this is a fast-forward.

gold.evidence: Git simplifies things by moving the pointer forward because there is no divergent work to merge together

question: A branch still has unmerged work and `git branch -d` refuses to delete it. How can I delete it anyway?
expected_answer: Force the deletion with `git branch -D <branch>` (the work is lost).

gold.evidence: If you really do want to delete the branch and lose that work, you can force it with `-D`

question: Which protocols can Git use to transfer data?
expected_answer: Local, HTTP, SSH and the Git protocol.

gold.evidence: Git can use four distinct protocols to transfer data: Local, HTTP, Secure Shell (SSH) and Git.

question: In a .gitignore file, what does starting a pattern with a forward slash do?
expected_answer: It avoids recursivity (pattern applies only at that level).

gold.evidence: You can start patterns with a forward slash (`/`) to avoid recursivity.

question: What are the main units of long-lived discussion in this tool?
expected_answer: Merge requests and issues (GitLab).

gold.evidence: Merge requests and issues are the main units of long-lived discussion in GitLab.

expected_answer: The Integration-Manager workflow.

question: How many API requests per hour can I make to GitHub with and without authenticating?
expected_answer: 60 per hour unauthenticated; up to 5,000 per hour when authenticated.

gold.evidence: Without authenticating, you will be limited to 60 requests per hour. If you authenticate you can make up to 5,000 requests per hour.

question: How do I give other people push access to my repository?
expected_answer: Add them as collaborators in the repository settings.

expected_answer: Integration managers in charge of certain parts of the repository.

question: What option must git describe be given to also use non-annotated tags?
expected_answer: The `--tags` option.

gold.evidence: if you want to take advantage of lightweight (non-annotated) tags as well, add the `--tags` option to the command.

question: How can I make a Git alias that runs an external program such as gitk instead of a Git subcommand?
expected_answer: Start the alias command with a `!` character, e.g. `git config --global alias.visual '!gitk'`.

gold.evidence: In that case, you start the command with a `!` character.

question: What does running git init create inside the project directory?
expected_answer: A new subdirectory named `.git` containing all the necessary repository files (a Git repository skeleton); nothing is tracked yet.

gold.evidence: This creates a new subdirectory named `.git` that contains all of your necessary repository files

question: If I protect my SSH key with a passphrase, which ssh-keygen option should I add and why?
expected_answer: Add the `-o` option; it saves the private key in a format more resistant to brute-force password cracking than the default.

gold.evidence: if you do use a password, make sure to add the `-o` option; it saves the private key in a format that is more resistant to brute-force password cracking

question: On which port does git instaweb start its temporary web server?
expected_answer: Port 1234 (it then opens a web browser on that page).

gold.evidence: That starts up an HTTPD server on port 1234

question: With Smart HTTP, if the GIT_HTTP_EXPORT_ALL variable is left out, which repositories are served to unauthenticated clients?
expected_answer: Only repositories that contain the `git-daemon-export-ok` file, just like the Git daemon.

gold.evidence: If you leave out `GIT_HTTP_EXPORT_ALL` environment variable, then Git will only serve to unauthenticated clients the repositories with the `git-daemon-export-ok` file in them

question: How do I show only the commits from the last two weeks in the log?
expected_answer: Use a time-limiting option: `git log --since=2.weeks`.

gold.evidence: this command gets the list of commits made in the last two weeks

question: Under what condition is a GitHub organization free?

question: When you clone a repository, what name does Git give the remote by default?
